we introduce a notion of optimality for interpolators in linear regression, derive a closed-form expression of the optimal response-linear interpolator, and provide a characterization of the regime where the optimal interpolator is provably better than the minimum-norm one.

The main takeaway from our work is that

there is no single interpolator that is provably optimal in the sense that it achieves optimal generalization for all data-generating distributions and that the optimal interpolator is a function of the data-generating distribution and the training data.

interpolating methods that are response-linear and depend on the training data, population covariance and signal-to-noise-ratio but not on the signal itself and the noise in the data are optimal in a sense that we introduce and can achieve this notion of optimally in a variety of settings.
